pageData.heading:
Understanding Home Buying Costs:
A Guide for Loan DSAs
pageData.para: Many home loan applicants focus only on the property's purchase price, overlooking additional expenses such as stamp duty, registration charges, legal fees, and other transaction costs. As a DSA, helping clients understand these expenses early improves financial preparedness, reduces funding gaps, and increases the likelihood of successful home loan approvals.

contents.heading: Property Purchase Costs Every DSA Should Explain
contents.listTopPara: Apart from the home loan amount, clients should be prepared for several government charges and statutory fees that can affect their overall funding requirement:

list.heading: Stamp Duty:
list.desc:
Stamp duty is one of the largest upfront costs associated with purchasing a property. It is levied by the state government and is calculated on the property's market value or purchase price, whichever is higher. Rates vary across states and typically range between 5% and 7%.

💡 DSA Insight: Always include stamp duty while estimating the client's total funding requirement, as it is generally not financed under the home loan.

💡 Note: Some states offer concessions or rebates for eligible homebuyers. Clients should verify the latest benefits applicable in their state.

list.heading: Property Registration Charges:
list.desc:
Registration charges are payable to legally register the property in the buyer's name. These charges are generally around 1% of the property's value, depending on state regulations.

💡 DSA Insight: Registration charges should be considered while assessing the client's total upfront expenses.

list.heading: Goods and Services Tax (GST):
list.desc:
GST applies only to eligible under-construction properties.

  • 1% for affordable housing.
  • 5% for non-affordable housing.

✅ Ready-to-move and completed properties are generally exempt from GST.

💡 DSA Insight: Understanding GST applicability helps you estimate the client's actual property acquisition cost and recommend suitable funding solutions.

contents.heading: Property Verification & Valuation
contents.listTopPara: Property verification and valuation play a critical role in home loan approvals. As a DSA, ensuring these checks are completed early can reduce processing delays and improve lender confidence.

list.heading: Legal & Technical Verification:
list.desc:
Verify that the property has a clear title, valid ownership records, and all necessary statutory approvals. Documents such as the sale deed, encumbrance certificate, approved building plans, and RERA registration (where applicable) should be reviewed before loan submission.

💡 DSA Insight: Early legal and technical verification helps minimize rejection risks and avoids delays during lender due diligence.

list.heading: Property Valuation:
list.desc:
Lenders conduct property valuations to determine the property's market value and calculate the eligible loan amount based on their Loan-to-Value (LTV) policy. An accurate valuation ensures the loan request aligns with lender guidelines.

💡 DSA Insight: Understanding the property's estimated market value helps you set realistic loan expectations and identify the most suitable lender for your client.

insurance.heading: Insurance Solutions for Home Loan Customers
insurance.listTopPara: Insurance products can strengthen a home loan offering by protecting borrowers against unforeseen events while providing additional financial security throughout the loan tenure.

list.heading: Home Loan Protection Insurance:
list.desc: Home loan protection insurance helps cover the outstanding loan amount in the event of the borrower's death, permanent disability, or other covered circumstances. As a DSA, informing eligible clients about this option can help them safeguard their family's financial future while ensuring continuity of loan repayment.

list.heading: Home Insurance:
list.desc: Home insurance protects the property against risks such as fire, theft, natural disasters, and other covered damages. Advising clients to secure appropriate property insurance helps preserve the value of their asset and provides additional peace of mind after loan disbursement.

legal.heading: Legal & Professional Services
legal.listTopPara: Legal and professional services play an important role in ensuring a smooth property transaction and home loan approval process. Understanding these requirements helps DSAs prepare clients and minimize delays.

list.heading: Property Documentation Support:
list.desc: Ensure all property documents, ownership records, approvals, and agreements are complete and legally compliant before submitting the loan application.

list.heading: Legal Verification:
list.desc: Lenders may conduct legal due diligence to verify the property's title, ownership history, and statutory approvals. Early verification helps reduce processing delays and strengthens the loan application.

list.heading: Professional Charges:
list.desc: Clients should also consider applicable legal, documentation, and professional service charges as part of their overall property purchase budget.

moving.heading: Additional Costs Clients Should Plan For
moving.listTopPara: Beyond the home loan and property purchase costs, clients should also be aware of post-purchase expenses that can impact their overall financial planning.

list.heading: Moving & Relocation Expenses:
list.desc: Clients may incur costs for packing, transportation, and relocation when moving into their new property. These expenses should be considered while planning the overall budget.

list.heading: Utility & Service Connections:
list.desc: Initial setup charges for electricity, water, gas, broadband, DTH, and other essential services may apply after possession.

list.heading: Property Maintenance & Municipal Charges:
list.desc: Recurring expenses such as municipal taxes, society maintenance charges, parking fees, and other community-related costs should be factored into the client's monthly budget.

list.heading: Interior & Home Setup:
list.desc: Depending on the property's condition, clients may need to budget for furniture, appliances, modular kitchens, wardrobes, lighting, or other interior improvements after possession.

loanCosts.heading: Home Loan Charges Clients Should Know
loanCosts.listTopPara: Apart from EMIs, clients should understand the lender-related charges that may apply during the home loan process:

list.heading: Loan Processing Charges:
list.desc: Most lenders charge a processing fee for evaluating and processing the loan application. The applicable amount varies by lender and loan product.

list.heading: Pre-EMI Interest:
list.desc: For under-construction properties, lenders may disburse the loan in stages. During this period, clients may be required to pay interest only on the amount already disbursed until full loan disbursement.

list.heading: Other Lender Charges:
list.desc: Additional charges such as legal verification fees, technical valuation fees, documentation charges, and other administrative costs may apply depending on the lender.

loanCosts.listSecPara: 💡 DSA Tip: Use DigitalDSA's eligibility calculators and planning tools to estimate borrowing capacity, compare lender offerings, and help clients understand the total cost of their home loan before applying.

subsidy.heading: Government Housing Schemes
subsidy.secPara:
Eligible customers may benefit from government-supported housing schemes, subsidies, or affordable housing initiatives based on prevailing policies and lender participation. As a DSA, understanding these programs can help you identify suitable opportunities for eligible clients and recommend the most appropriate financing solution.

✅ Always verify the latest eligibility criteria and scheme availability with the participating lender or the relevant government authority.
